verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second-round review 2026-10-06. Re-fetched both sources. News page: 'Publication 29 September 2026' (event_date correct); 'The consultation remains open until 3 November 2026'; four areas quoted correctly and in order; stakeholder sentence includes 'generative AI providers and other relevant actors in the AI value chain'; builds on a call for evidence held earlier this year. All first-round fixes applied. EUSurvey page loads: title 'Targeted consultation on a potential initiative for a better copyright environment for European creativity and innovation'; sections include three on copyright and generative AI (including licensing/enforcement and AI-generated imitations of performers), piracy, sound recordings of non-EU nationals, and research; question text did not render, so the summary's caveat is accurate. Primary tier and medium confidence are appropriate. Not a duplicate: the only copyright hit is eu-gpai-code-of-practice.json, a different instrument. Tone is neutral. WRONG: (1) why_it_matters says 'as it applies to AI training'; 'training' appears in neither source, which say 'use of copyright-protected content in artificial intelligence' and 'generative AI'. This is an inferred narrowing, so claim_matches_source fails; the 'training data' topic has the same weaker problem. (2) gaps[0] still says the consultation document was not fetched, which contradicts the item. (3) Minor: 'feedback deadline' vs the page's 'remains open until'.
required_changes: In why_it_matters, replace 'as it applies to AI training' with 'as it applies to the use of copyright-protected content in AI'.
Replace or drop the 'training data' topic unless source text mentioning training is cited.
Update gaps[0]: the EUSurvey page was fetched (title and section headings read, questions not rendered) and the Have Your Say page was not fetched.
Optional: change 'The page gives a feedback deadline of 3 November 2026' to 'The page states the consultation remains open until 3 November 2026'.
